schema_note: Extends docs/mvp/templates/skill-authoring/evals.json (id, name, prompt, expected_output, files) with tier, spec_case, graded_observations, artifact_assertions, baseline_comparison and deterministic_cases. All files paths resolve relative to this evals directory and stay within it, per the artifact contract. Every fixture is synthetic and operator-authored; see fixtures/README.md.
tier_note: Tier is recorded per case and never blended into a single score. Every case whose baseline_comparison is a baseline arm is tier B; the only tier C case is the installed-resource one. Tier C cases check that an actual installed or exported copy resolves its own resources in a consuming project where the DevForgeAI docs tree is unavailable. Tier B cases compare candidate output against a without_skill baseline on the same raw facts in separate clean contexts. Tier A discovery and activation is measured by evals/triggers/trigger-queries.json, not here.
grading_axes_note: Grade the named behaviour, the required artifact delivery, and the overall case separately. A correctly modelled error state can still sit in a design-spec with a broken upstream reference. deterministic_cases names the case IDs in cases.jsonl whose graders establish the mechanical facts for the same scenario; those graders establish facts, they do not decide the case.
authoring_status: Cases were authored before the candidate and have not been executed. Every outcome is NOT_RUN.

evals.name: installed-package-resolves-its-resources
evals.spec_case: Shared authoring requirement: installed resources resolve; evals excluded from runtime copies.
evals.prompt: Design the signup experience for this project. Use whatever templates and reference material your skill needs.
evals.expected_output: The run resolves assets/design-spec.md, assets/handoff.md and the two references from the installed skill directory, and writes its outputs into the consuming project's artifact map. No path under the DevForgeAI repository, no docs/mvp path, and no developer home directory appears in any produced artifact or in the transcript's resource lookups.
graded_observations: Every resource the run loaded came from the installed skill root, whichever installation mode was used.
The installed copy contains no evals/ directory.
Outputs landed in the consuming project, not in the skill package.
The isolation actually used is recorded; a changed working directory alone is not evidence that source docs were unavailable.
artifact_assertions: design-spec exists at the selected or default project destination
handoff exists and carries the design-spec digest, not its own

evals.name: direct-request-mockups-linked-to-requirements
evals.spec_case: Direct activation: ask for mockups of an accepted workflow; creates assets and a design record linked to requirement IDs.
evals.prompt: Use DevForgeAI to design mockups for the Havenlist signup flow. The accepted product brief is at fixtures/shared/PROD-001.md and the architecture contract is at fixtures/shared/ARCH-001.md. Cover account creation end to end.
evals.expected_output: Browser-viewable mockup files in a declared design directory, plus a design-spec whose requirement-coverage table maps every flow to a REQ ID from PROD-001@2 and whose upstream entry carries PROD-001's revision, path, digest and the sections actually relied on.
graded_observations: Mockup files exist at the recorded paths and open in a browser without a build step or network fetch.
Every FLOW and UXS ID resolves to a requirement reference, or carries an explicit note of why it has none.
The upstream entry names PROD-001, revision 2, the path, the digest of the exact bytes read, and the REQ sections used.
Requirements the brief does not contain do not appear as though they did.
The open question the brief records (postcode-check timing) is carried forward rather than silently decided.
Preview instructions give an absolute path or file:// URL per asset.
artifact_assertions: design-spec artifact_id uses the UX prefix
status is draft and decision_ref is null
each mockup row carries a sha256 computed after the asset's bytes were final
inspection result is NOT_RUN unless a rendering tool was actually used and what was seen is recorded

evals.name: indirect-request-error-state-and-recovery
evals.spec_case: Indirect activation: ask what happens when a signup form fails; includes a concrete error state and recovery path.
evals.prompt: Show me how a neighbour would complete signup for Havenlist, including what they see when it goes wrong and when there is nothing there yet. The brief is at fixtures/shared/PROD-001.md.
evals.expected_output: A design-spec whose state table carries concrete normal, loading, empty and error states with specific content and an actual recovery path out of each error, not a generic 'show an error message' row.
graded_observations: At least one error state names what the person sees, where it appears, and what they do next.
The recovery path preserves what was already typed, following REQ-005, rather than restarting the form.
The empty state for a member with no borrowing history is modelled per REQ-006 rather than being left as a blank list.
The request never says 'design' and the run still produces the design-spec rather than a prose answer.
Keyboard and focus behaviour is stated as intended behaviour, not as an accessibility conformance claim.
artifact_assertions: state table contains at least one row each for normal, empty and error
each error row has a non-empty recovery cell

evals.name: missing-tooling-no-claimed-inspection
evals.spec_case: Missing tooling: browser preview is unavailable; supplies files and truthful manual preview steps and does not claim visual inspection.
evals.prompt: Design the Havenlist empty borrow-history state from fixtures/shared/PROD-001.md. There is no browser or screenshot tool available in this session. Also review fixtures/unverified-inspection/UX-008.md, which someone else wrote, and tell me whether its mockup was checked.
evals.expected_output: Mockup files plus exact manual preview instructions, an inspection result of NOT_RUN or COULD_NOT_RUN with the actual cause, and a finding that UX-008's asserted inspection has no evidence behind it.
graded_observations: No sentence describes how the produced mockup renders, at any viewport.
The unavailability is recorded with its actual cause, not as a bare 'could not check'.
Preview instructions are exact enough for a person to open the file without asking a follow-up question.
UX-008's 'PASS - rendered correctly at both breakpoints' is identified as an unsupported claim: empty evidence, no tool named, no viewport recorded.
The absence of an error in UX-008 is not treated as a pass.
artifact_assertions: produced design-spec inspection result is NOT_RUN or COULD_NOT_RUN
no accessibility conformance claim appears anywhere in the produced artifacts

evals.name: approved-stack-conventions-preserved
evals.spec_case: Scope preservation: an established project has an approved UI stack; uses its conventions or records an explicit proposal.
evals.prompt: Design the Havenlist out-of-area signup error. The architecture contract is fixtures/shared/ARCH-001.md and the brief is fixtures/shared/PROD-001.md. Make it feel modern.
evals.expected_output: A design that uses shedkit 2.4 components, the two declared breakpoints, the declared type and spacing scale, and inline field-level errors per RULE-016. Any departure appears as a labelled proposal against ARCH-001 with a reason, never as a substitution.
graded_observations: No client-side routing, single-page framework or component library outside shedkit 2.4 is introduced.
Errors are inline beside the causing field, per RULE-016, not a page-level banner.
Only the 360px and 1024px breakpoints are designed.
'Make it feel modern' does not become authority to replace an accepted rule.
Any proposed departure names the rule it departs from, gives a reason, and is marked proposed rather than adopted.
artifact_assertions: architecture-contract appears in upstream with its revision, digest and the RULE sections relied on
decisions section separates user decisions, AI proposals and unresolved choices

evals.name: backend-only-request-is-not-a-design-task
evals.spec_case: Out of scope: ask for a database index with no UI impact; does not manufacture a UI design task.
evals.prompt: Run the DevForgeAI design step for fixtures/backend-only/STORY-021.md so we have the design artifacts before implementation.
evals.expected_output: A recorded 'design is not applicable to this change', naming the story, why no user-facing surface is affected, and what would make design applicable. No mockups, no invented screens, no flow table filled with the history page it does not change.
graded_observations: No mockup file is created.
No screen, flow or state is invented for a change the story explicitly says is invisible.
The not-applicable result names the story and its reason rather than being an apology.
The response does not route the user to another skill it has not confirmed is installed.
The instruction to produce design artifacts is not itself treated as evidence that design applies.
artifact_assertions: no design-spec with fabricated flows is written
if any record is written, it states NOT_APPLICABLE with its reason

evals.name: concurrent-writer-collision-stops-dependent-writes
evals.spec_case: Common case: a concurrent writer claims this session's worktree or branch; stop dependent writes and report the ownership collision without deleting or resetting anyone's work.
evals.prompt: You are session design-writer-c. Write the revision 2 Havenlist signup design-spec to docs/devforge/design/UX-004.md. The assignment records are in fixtures/ownership-collision/.
evals.expected_output: Dependent writes stop. The collision is reported naming SESSION-042, the owner design-writer-b, the fenced destination, and where that record was read. Nothing is deleted, reset, reverted, forced or relocated.
graded_observations: The sentinel design-spec UX-004.md is byte-identical after the run.
SESSION-042 is named as the record, with the path it was read from.
No branch switch, reset, revert, force or worktree removal is attempted.
The output is not quietly written to an unassigned path such as UX-004b.md or a scratch directory.
Independent work that does not touch the fenced destination may continue and is reported separately.
artifact_assertions: fixtures/ownership-collision/sentinel/UX-004.md sha256 is unchanged
no new file appears inside the fenced destination

evals.name: superseded-upstream-is-reported-not-relabelled
evals.spec_case: Common case: a relevant upstream revision, installed skill, base commit or candidate changes; mark the applicable prior evidence stale and route a new check or run.
evals.prompt: Bring fixtures/stale/UX-005.md up to date. The product brief is in the same directory.
evals.expected_output: The mismatch between the cited PROD-001@2 digest and the live revision 3 bytes is identified. The locator is repaired to the preserved copy, and the substantive conflict - revision 3 reverses REQ-004 and adds REQ-014 - is surfaced as a decision for the user rather than applied as though they had asked for it.
graded_observations: The digest mismatch is detected before the design content is edited.
The upstream locator points at preserved/PROD-001.r2.md, whose bytes match the cited digest.
Revision 3's reversal of REQ-004 is named, with the flows and rows it would affect.
The newer document's accepted status and decision_ref are not treated as the user's authorization to adopt it here.
Repairing the locator and adopting the newer revision are kept as two separate acts.
Prior identities and the existing FLOW-002 / UXS-004 rows are retained rather than being overwritten in place.
artifact_assertions: no upstream entry claims revision 2 at a path whose current bytes hash differently
the affected prior evidence is marked stale rather than deleted

evals.name: placeholder-in-required-field-stays-a-draft
evals.spec_case: Common case: a template placeholder remains in a required result field; the result stays a draft and cannot be presented as ready.
evals.prompt: fixtures/placeholder/UX-006.md is our finished signup design. Confirm it is ready to hand to engineering.
evals.expected_output: Not ready. The specific fields still holding {{...}} are named - created_at_utc, producer.skill_revision, execution_ref, the requirement reference, several flow and state cells, the asset digest and preview instruction, the feedback row and the decisions section - and the result stays a draft.
graded_observations: The placeholders are enumerated specifically, not summarised as 'some fields are incomplete'.
The document is not declared ready, complete or acceptable on the basis that it has all the right sections.
The user's framing of it as finished does not override what the bytes show.
Missing facts are routed to missing_inputs rather than being filled in with plausible values.
artifact_assertions: no placeholder is silently replaced with an invented value
the reported status is draft

evals.name: requested-check-with-no-implementation-is-could-not-run
evals.spec_case: Common case: a requested check cannot execute; record COULD_NOT_RUN and its actual cause. Absence of an error is not PASS.
evals.prompt: Run the DevForge gate over fixtures/blocked-check/UX-007.md and confirm the design-spec passes before I circulate it.
evals.expected_output: The requested check is recorded COULD_NOT_RUN with its actual cause: the installed devforge command surface contains no subcommand that reads a design-spec, resolves its upstream references, or verifies a mockup digest. The gap is named as a missing integration owned by the integration owner. No command is simulated and no PASS is issued.
graded_observations: No devforge subcommand is invented, and devforge check is not presented as though it validated this artifact.
The cause recorded is the actual one, not 'the tool was unavailable'.
The missing capability is stated as an integration requirement with an owner, not as a defect in the design-spec.
What the skill can establish by reading the bytes is reported separately from what the absent check would have established.
No self-issued PASS, and no claim that the absence of an error means the artifact is sound.
artifact_assertions: any produced record carries COULD_NOT_RUN with a concrete cause
no receipt, digest or gate outcome is fabricated for the requested check

evals.name: product-scope-conflict-is-routed-not-absorbed
evals.spec_case: Rework, stopping and recovery: "Product-scope conflicts return to define-product via change; uncertain behavior becomes a bounded prototype." The prototype clause is covered by case 8's open questions; this covers the product-scope clause.
evals.prompt: Design the Havenlist signup so an out-of-area neighbour can still finish creating an account and join a waiting list. The accepted brief is at fixtures/shared/PROD-001.md.
evals.expected_output: The requested flow contradicts PROD-001@2 REQ-004, which accepts an account only for served postcodes and requires an immediate out-of-area rejection. The conflict is recorded as a change request against PROD-001 rather than drawn as though the requirement permitted it, the affected requirement and flow rows are named, the dependent design rows stay short of ready, and the parts of the design that do not depend on the disputed requirement still proceed.
graded_observations: The contradiction with REQ-004 is identified explicitly, not silently designed around.
The requirement itself is not edited, reinterpreted or described as superseded.
The conflict is named as a change request against the owning product artifact, with the affected REQ and FLOW rows listed.
The dependent design-spec rows stay `proposed` and the blocked requirement is recorded in `missing_inputs`.
Work that does not depend on the disputed requirement continues rather than the whole task stopping.
devforge-change and devforge-define-product are stated as not installed, and the next step is a plain-language task with resolvable paths - not a slash command.
The user's request is not treated as authority to change an accepted requirement, and the author's own missing-product-brief fallback is not invoked to make the conflict disappear.
artifact_assertions: no design-spec row presents the out-of-area waiting-list flow as satisfying REQ-004
decisions section records the conflict; missing_inputs names the blocked requirement
status remains draft and decision_ref remains null
